title: All or nothing
description:
`replaceAll` is supposed to replace the contents of `target` with `source`, but only if every entry in `source` is valid (not empty). It throws `std::invalid_argument` at the first empty entry.

The trouble is that it has already changed `target` by then. After the exception, `target` is half old, half new: neither what the caller had nor what they asked for.

Rewrite it to give the **strong guarantee**: if it throws, `target` is exactly as it was. The recipe is to do all the work that might fail on a separate copy, and only then swap it in (swapping cannot fail).
hints: Build the new contents in a local copy first, checking every entry as you go; an exception then leaves `target` untouched.
Only after the loop has finished, `target.swap(copy);` (or `std::swap`): swapping cannot throw.
